source_text:
τοὺς ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐν αὐτῇ συναγείρεσθαι. Γένοιτο δ' ἂν καὶ τοῦτο σημεῖον, τοῦ δεῖν ἅπαντας τοὺς οἵπερ ἂν εἶεν τὸν εὐκλεᾶ καὶ εὐδόκιμον διαζήσαντες βίον, εἰς τὴν ἄνω συλλέγεσθαι πόλιν, τὴν ἐπουράνιον Ἱερουσαλὴμ, ἐκεῖ καὶ συνεσομένους καὶ συνεορτάσοντας τῷ Χριστῷ· τοῖς δὲ ἀπίστοις ἔτι, καὶ τὴν τῆς ἀναστάσεως χάριν οὐ προσιεμένοις, ἠθετηκόσι δὲ μᾶλλον τὸ οὕτω σεπτὸν καὶ βαθὺ μυστήριον, ὄλεθρος μὲν ἡ δίκη, τότε ἐν παντὶ γενέσθαι κακῷ πάντη τε καὶ πάντως, ἀποκείσεται. Κατοιχήσονται γὰρ εἰς κόλασιν. Καὶ μάρτυς ἂν γένοιτο τοῦ τοιοῦδε πιστὸς ὁ προφήτης Ζαχαρίας, λέγων· «Καὶ ἔσται ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ ἀναβῶσιν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν φυλῶν τῆς γῆς εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ τοῦ προσκυνῆσαι τῷ Βασιλεῖ Κυρίῳ παντοκράτορι καὶ οὗτοι ἐκείνοις προστεθήσονται. Ἐὰν δὲ φυλὴ Αἰγύπτου μὴ ἀναβῇ, μηδὲ ἐξέλθῃ ἐκεῖ, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτοις ἔσται ἡ πτῶσις, ἣν ἂν πατάξῃ Κύριος πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ὃς ἐὰν μὴ ἀναβῇ τοῦ ἑορτάσαι τὴν ἑορτὴν τῆς Σκηνοπηγίας.» Σκηνοπηγίας οὖν ἄρα τριπόθητον ἑορτὴν καταλογιούμεθά που, τὴν τῶν σωμάτων ἁπάντων ἀνάστασιν, ἀπαρχὴν ἐχόντων Χριστόν· πρωτότοκος γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν κεχρημάτικε, καὶ ἔστιν ἀληθῶς.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθότατα διανοῇ.
{ΚΥΡ.} Πλὴν ἐκεῖνο ἴσθι τοι.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ ποῖον τί φής;
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἐν μὲν γὰρ τοῖς ἀρτίως ἡμῖν παρενηνεγμένοις τοῦ νόμου λογίοις, ὠνόμασται μὲν ἐνδελεχισμοῦ θυσία, καὶ μέν τοι καὶ νουμηνία, καὶ τὰ ἐν Σαββάτοις ἱερὰ καὶ μὲν καὶ ἡ νηστεία, καὶ προσέτι τῆς Σκηνοπηγίας ἡ πολύευκτος ἑορτή. Προσετίθει δὲ πανταχῆ καὶ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν εἰρημένων ὁ νόμος, τὸ «Προσοίσετε ὁλοκαυτώματα τῷ Κυρίῳ.» Καὶ τίνες δ' ἂν γένοιντο πρὸς ἡμῶν τῶν θυσιῶν οἱ τρόποι, οἵ τε τῇ νεομηνίᾳ πρέποντες, καὶ μὴν καὶ Σαββάτοις νηστεία δὲ αὖ καὶ οἱ κατ' αὐτὴν ἐσόμενοι τὴν Σκηνοπηγίαν ἢ ὅ τί ποτέ ἐστι τὸ εἰς θυσίαν ἐνδελεχὲς, σεσίγηκε μὲν ὁ νομοθετῶν ἐν τῷ Λευιτικῷ, κατευρύνει δὲ ὥσπερ τὸν ἐπὶ τοῖσδε λόγον, καὶ σὺν πολλῇ λίαν ἰσχνομυθίᾳ συντέθεικεν ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς· βούλει λέγωμεν ἀνὰ μέρος ἕκαστα διαλαβόντες, ὡς ἔνι;
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν.
{ΚΥΡ.} Γέγραπται τοίνυν ὡδί· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Ἔντειλαι τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτοὺς, λέγων· Τὰ δῶρά μου, δόματά μου, καρπωματά μου εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας διατηρήσετε προσφέρειν ἐμοὶ ἐν ταῖς ἑορταῖς μου. Καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ταῦτα τὰ καρπώματα ὅσα προσάξετε Κυρίῳ, ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἀμώμους δύο τὴν ἡμέραν εἰς ὁλοκαύτωσιν ἐνδελεχῶς. Τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν ἕνα ποιήσεις τὸ πρωΐ, καὶ τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν δεύτερον ποιήσεις τὸ πρὸς ἑσπέραν, καὶ ποιήσεις τὸ δέκατον τοῦ οἰφὶ σεμίδαλιν εἰς θυσίαν ἀναπεποιημένην ἐν ἐλαίῳ ἐν τετάρτῳ τοῦ ἴν. Ὁλοκαύτωμα ἐνδελεχισμοῦ, ἡ γενομένη θυσία ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ. Καὶ σπονδὴν αὐτῷ τὸ τέταρτον τοῦ ἲν τῷ ἀμνῷ τῶν ἑνὶ, ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ [αλ. ἀγγείῳ] σπεί
pass_a_gloss: (it was necessity) for those from all Judea to be gathered in it. And this too would be a sign of the need that all who have lived the glorious and well-approved life be collected into the city above, the heavenly Jerusalem, there both to be together with and to feast together with Christ; but for those still unbelieving, and not admitting the grace of the resurrection, but rather having set aside the so august and deep mystery, destruction is the penalty, to come to be then in every evil wholly and altogether, it will be laid up. For they will go down into punishment. And a faithful witness of such a thing would be the prophet Zechariah, saying: 'And it will be, whoever do not go up from all the tribes of the earth to Jerusalem to worship the King, Lord Almighty, these too will be added to those. And if the tribe of Egypt does not go up nor come out there, upon these also will be the fall, with which the Lord will strike all the nations, whoever does not go up to feast the feast of Tent-pitching.' So then we shall reckon somewhere the thrice-longed-for feast of Tent-pitching to be the resurrection of all bodies, having Christ as firstfruits; for firstborn from the dead he has been styled, and is truly. PALL.: Most rightly you think. CYR.: Except know that thing. PALL.: What sort, what do you say? CYR.: For in the oracles of the law just brought forward by us there have been named the sacrifice of continuance, and also the new moon, and the sacred things on Sabbaths, and also the fast, and besides the much-prayed-for feast of Tent-pitching. And the law added everywhere and upon each of the things said: 'You will offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord.' And what the ways of the sacrifices would be for us, both those fitting the new moon, and also for Sabbaths, and again the fast, and those that will be at the Tent-pitching itself, or whatever the continual thing for sacrifice is, the lawgiver kept silent in Leviticus, but he broadens as it were the account about these, and has composed with very much fine detail in Numbers; do you wish that we speak taking up each in part, as is possible? PALL.: Altogether so. CYR.: It is written then thus: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the sons of Israel and you will say to them, saying: My gifts, my presents, my offerings for an odor of fragrance you will keep to offer to me in my feasts. And you will say to them: These are the offerings which you will bring to the Lord: lambs a year old, unblemished, two a day, for a whole burnt offering continually. The one lamb you will do in the morning, and the second lamb you will do toward evening, and you will do the tenth of the ephah of fine flour for a sacrifice mixed in oil in a fourth of the hin. A whole burnt offering of continuance, the sacrifice made on mount Sinai for an odor of fragrance to the Lord. And its libation, the fourth of the hin for the one lamb, in the holy place [another reading: vessel] you will pou(r) (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …for those from all Judea to gather in it. This too would be a sign that all who have lived a glorious and well-approved life must be gathered into the city above, the heavenly Jerusalem (Hebrews 12:22), to be with Christ there and to keep the feast with him. But for those who are still unbelieving, who do not accept the grace of the resurrection but have rather set aside so august and deep a mystery, destruction is the penalty laid up: to be in every evil then, wholly and altogether. For they will go down into punishment. And the prophet Zechariah would be a faithful witness to this, when he says, ‘And it shall be that whoever of all the tribes of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, they too shall be added to those. And if the tribe of Egypt does not go up nor come there, upon them too shall be the fall with which the Lord will strike all the nations, whoever does not go up to keep the feast of Tabernacles’ (Zechariah 14:17–18). So we shall reckon the thrice-longed-for feast of Tabernacles to be, I suppose, the resurrection of all bodies, which have Christ as their firstfruits. For he has been called the firstborn from the dead (Colossians 1:18), and he truly is.
Palladius: Your thought is most correct.
Cyril: But know this, at least.
Palladius: What is that? What do you mean?

Cyril: In the oracles of the law that we have just brought forward, there are named the continual sacrifice, and the new moon too, and the sacred rites on the sabbaths, and also the fast, and besides these the much-desired feast of Tabernacles. And everywhere, with each of the things named, the law added, ‘You shall offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord.’ But what the manner of our sacrifices should be, those fitting for the new moon, and for the sabbaths too, and for the fast, and those to be offered at the feast of Tabernacles itself, or what exactly the continual sacrifice is, the lawgiver passed over in silence in Leviticus. In Numbers, however, he broadens the account of these things, as it were, and has set it out in very fine detail. Shall we take each of them in turn, as far as we can, and speak of it?

Cyril: It is written as follows (Numbers 28:1–7): ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the sons of Israel, and say to them: My gifts, my presents, my offerings for a fragrant aroma you shall take care to offer to me at my feasts. And you shall say to them: These are the offerings that you shall bring to the Lord: two unblemished lambs a year old each day, as a continual whole burnt offering. The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer toward evening; and you shall offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sacrifice, mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil. It is a continual whole burnt offering, the sacrifice that was made on Mount Sinai for a fragrant aroma to the Lord. And its drink offering, a quarter of a hin for each lamb; in the holy place you shall pour…

choices.why: ἰσχνός, fine or spare; the point is exactness in Numbers against silence in Leviticus.
